title: Pressing and Must
body: Must is the intermediate product between grapes and wine. Add grapes to a grape press one at a time, then use the press with an empty hand when at least four compatible grapes are ready. Each pressing uses four grapes and produces must.
Use an empty glass bottle on the press to collect the must. Continue pressing and bottling as capacity allows, then take the bottled must to a fermentation barrel.

Keep compatible grapes and batches together. Matching colour alone does not mean every grape or must stack can be combined: their recorded batch and quality information also matters. If the press refuses an addition or a pressing, check its feedback and finish collecting the existing output before starting another batch.
Pressing carries the grapes' identity and quality into the next stage. It is the beginning of winemaking, not the end of the vineyard's influence on the bottle.
